paul-docs: Heads up my PR (refs: #489) failed the docs CI with an odd duplicate-id error referencing an auto-generated MDX anchor. Works locally for me but CI errors out. Anyone seen MDX heading ids go strange after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration? builder-bot: builder-bot: docs-site: build failed: Error: duplicate id 'deploying' at /docs/ops/deploying.mdx:45 harper-web: We hit similar before. Docusaurus/MDX will auto-generate an id from the heading text, but our migration added a couple of files with the same short page title "Deploying" and different filenames. On the site build those collapse to the same anchor if the filename-based prefix isn't applied consistently. paul-docs: Interesting. The two files are `ops/deploying.mdx` and `getting-started/deploying.mdx`. Locally I see anchors `getting-started-deploying` and `ops-deploying`, but on CI both end up `deploying`. kai-infra: CI runs the container build that uses a different MDX plugin pipeline (we added a quick compat shim during migration). The shim strips filename prefixes, which explains why both get the bare heading slug. I can roll back that shim but we should either keep it or ensure unique ids. harper-web: Quick fixes: (A) add explicit HTML ids on the conflicting headings, e.g. "

Deploying

", or (B) set `remark-autolink-headings` / `remark-slug` options to include the relative path as a prefix. Option A is fastest for a single PR. lucy-qa: Also, our linkchecker currently flags cross-page anchor links as broken if the anchor doesn't match exactly. Linkcheck output: `linkcheck: 5 broken anchors, 1 dup-id`. It can produce false positives while we sort slug rules. paul-docs: I can add the explicit id in my PR and update any local cross-page links that target `#deploying`. That should unblock CI. kai-infra: I'll add a small CI lint step to detect duplicate ids earlier in the pipeline: `yarn docs:lint:anchors` that runs a Node script to parse built HTML and report identical ids across pages. That will fail fast before the full build. harper-web: Long term I'd prefer deterministic slugging that resembles GitHub's behavior: `slugify: s => require('github-slugger').slug(s)` + include the doc path in the generated id to avoid collisions for same heading across files. We can make it opt-in in the docusaurus config so it's explicit during migration. lucy-qa: One more hiccup: we have a couple of relative links that point into README fragments like `../README.md#quick-start`. After migration the target anchor changed (README title -> `quick-start-guide`). We should run a mapping script to rewrite those links. The linkchecker report lists them: `../README.md#quick-start -> 404 on site` paul-docs: Good catch. I'll search the repo for `#quick-start` and add redirects or update the links in affected docs. kai-infra: I'll open a small infra PR to (1) add the anchor-lint job, (2) print offending file+line when duplicate ids are found, and (3) add an optional `--dereference-symlinks` flag to the docs packaging step so shared assets don't 404 in CI. harper-web: Also propose a short migration checklist doc in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md outlining known gotchas: MDX auto-ids, relative README anchors, and how to opt into filename-prefixing for headings. That should help authors during future imports. lucy-qa: I'll run the linkchecker locally on Paul's branch once he pushes the explicit ids and I'll validate the cross-page links. :white_check_mark: paul-docs: Plan: (1) add explicit ids to the conflicting headings in my PR, (2) update any broken `#quick-start` links to the new anchors or add redirects, (3) follow up with infra and docs-config PRs for linting and slug normalization. Opening PR now and will ping when CI reruns. harper-web: Thanks 44d happy to review the docs-config change when you're ready. kai-infra: I'll draft the CI anchor-lint and the dereference packaging change today. lucy-qa: Ping me when CI is green, I'll do a quick smoke test and approve.
